name: Thimlich Ohinga Archaeological Site
description: Near the town of Migori in southwestern Kenya, Thimlich Ohinga is a ring of massive stone walls built without any mortar. Rough blocks interlock to form barriers up to about 4 metres high and 3 metres thick. Probably raised around the 16th century, it sheltered families and their livestock, and it is the largest and best preserved of many such enclosures around Lake Victoria.
